items.title: Radisson Adds Older Hotels and Meeting Spaces to Net Zero Program
items.summary: The four new Verified Net Zero Hotels are based in Stockholm and Copenhagen, reinforcing the scheme’s Nordic skew and highlighting a key bottleneck in scaling decarbonization: access to renewable energy.

items.title: Choice Hotels Buys RV Club Harvest Hosts for $130 Million
items.summary: Choice CEO Dom Dragisich will need to show that Harvest Hosts, a list of a half-million RV users, converts into hotel stays. Otherwise, he's drifting from the "top priority" he set after taking the job of driving net rooms growth.

items.title: The Travel Distribution Funnel Is Coming Apart
items.summary: AI is fragmenting travel distribution across many starting points instead of simply replacing Google with a new gatekeeper.

items.title: Accor’s Leire Leoz on Why Franchise Growth Has to Be Earned
items.summary: Accor is betting heavily on its franchise model, and the Group’s global chief franchise officer, Leire Leoz, says growth only works if owners see real value. Her focus is on hotel performance, stronger brand standards, simpler support, and giving franchisees more reasons to stay

items.title: Airbnb Launches AI Tools, Catching Up to OTA Rivals
items.summary: Airbnb is not a first-mover in AI launches. That's OK: Kayak wasn't a first-mover in metasearch. The issue isn't necessarily timing, but whether Airbnb can offer AI products that are better than its rivals.

items.title: Rotana CEO: Last-Minute Gulf Bookings Make Q4 Hard To Predict
items.summary: The expected return of international travelers and a busy events calendar give hope for a Q4 recovery.

items.title: Vrbo to Double Commissions as It Plays Catch-Up to Airbnb
items.summary: Airbnb and Booking.com charge no guest fees. But Vrbo has stated that it will keep guest fees, although the amounts will be flexible. That lack of specificity will stoke host anger because this gives hosts little visibility into the actual prices their guests will have to pay.

items.title: Hilton Tech Exec Says AI Agents Put OTAs ‘Under Real Threat’
items.summary: Hilton CIO Michael Leidinger believes the OTAs' decline will benefit hotels, even while conceding that AI agents will likely charge commissions, too. The difference is that Hilton will get more bookings on its site and app.
